html:
An ancient Roman aqueduct about 69 km long, begun by Caligula in 38 CE and finished by Claudius in 52 CE. It was the eighth aqueduct to supply Rome.

Its water came from springs in the upper Anio valley, east of the city. For the last stretch across the plain it ran on tall stone arches, sharing them with a second new aqueduct, the Anio Novus, which ran in a channel on top. The two crossed the roads into Rome over a grand double gate, now the Porta Maggiore, which still bears Claudius's inscription.

Nero built a branch on arches to carry its water to the Palatine Hill and his palace. The engineer Frontinus, who ran Rome's water supply around 97 CE, counted it with the Aqua Marcia among the finest of the city's aqueducts.

Long rows of its arches still stride across the countryside south-east of Rome, in what is now the Park of the Aqueducts, one of the most famous sights of the Roman Empire.
sum: An ancient Roman aqueduct about 69 km long, begun by Caligula in 38 CE and finished by Claudius in 52 CE. It was the eighth aqueduct to supply Rome.
